profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the Quebec Ministry of Justice and the university-based evaluation team to align the handoff for a briefing package on the Montreal parenting coordination pilot (2012-2014). The context is that the Ministry wants to prepare a Deputy Minister briefing and stakeholder note on what was learned from the pilot, while the research team is finalizing synthesis materials drawn from ten family files and coordinator interviews. The agenda is to confirm what goes into the shared briefing package, which case materials will be attached, how the section on integration with other services will be framed, and when the package will be circulated. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on deliverables, timing, and circulation of the briefing materials for the next implementation discussion.

members.name: Claire Bouchard
members.role: Senior Counsel, Family Justice Policy Directorate, Quebec Ministry of Justice
members.expertise: Family law reform, court-connected services, ministerial briefing preparation, privacy-sensitive legal policy drafting
members.background: Claire is a ministry lawyer who has worked on family justice access initiatives and inter-service coordination files involving courts, youth protection, and community providers in Quebec.
members.private_state: She wants a concise, decision-ready briefing that can safely move upward inside the Ministry without reopening methodological debates or creating privacy concerns around sensitive family narratives.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'recommendations,' they mean short policy actions that the Ministry could operationalize or test, not a full discussion of research caveats.
The 'pilot cohort' for reporting purposes is the subset of families with enough participation to support ministry-facing operational lessons, not every family initially enrolled.
An 'anonymized case summary' means the Ministry's one-page redacted service snapshot stored in the internal briefing folder.
The 'integration' section is about formal interfaces between parenting coordination and existing justice or publicly funded family services in Montreal.
Once a package is 'ready for circulation,' it is ready for internal government circulation through the Ministry's usual document format and secure channels.

members.name: Dr. Julien Martel
members.role: Research Coordinator, Interdisciplinary Parenting Coordination Evaluation Team
members.expertise: Socio-legal evaluation, family dispute systems, mixed-method pilot assessment, research synthesis across legal and psychosocial services
members.background: Julien coordinates the research team that followed the pilot families and worked with the two parenting coordinators to document outcomes, service interactions, and implementation lessons.
members.private_state: He wants the briefing materials to preserve the complexity of the pilot, including early exits and service-system limits, and he wants outside practitioners to validate the summaries before they are treated as settled findings.
hidden_assumptions: When people ask for 'recommendations,' they want the evidence-based lessons, limitations, and conditions for future scaling, not only ministry action items.
The 'pilot cohort' means all ten enrolled families because implementation learning includes withdrawals, partial participation, and difficult cases.
An 'anonymized case summary' means a de-identified narrative memo with chronology and service interactions that can be checked against coordinator notes.
The 'integration' section includes both public and private sector connections, including mediators, psychologists, and other referral pathways discussed during the pilot.
Once a package is 'ready for circulation,' it is ready to be shared with external pilot participants or partner professionals for factual validation before final use.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to finalize 'the recommendations' for the briefing package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a concise list of ministry-facing implementation actions and policy options suitable for an internal executive briefing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the broader recommendations section from the evaluation, including methodological cautions, service conditions, and cross-sector implications.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In legal-policy coordination, 'recommendations' is a routine closing deliverable, so both hear a familiar term and assume the other is referring to the standard version used in their own setting.

misalignment_points.topic: Which families are included in the pilot cohort
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the pilot families' or 'the ten files' when discussing examples and lessons learned.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is mentally centering the families with enough engagement to support operational reporting, effectively excluding the early-exit files from the core set she expects in the briefing narrative.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to all ten enrolled families, including the early withdrawals, because those cases inform feasibility and integration lessons.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both participants know the pilot involved ten families, so the label sounds settled; the divergence lies in which files each expects to actually anchor the synthesis, which feels too implicit to restate.

misalignment_points.topic: What an anonymized case summary is and how it is shared
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Julien will send over the 'anonymized case summaries' before circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects one-page redacted summaries in the Ministry's internal format, uploaded to the secure government workspace for internal use only.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects richer de-identified narrative summaries with service timelines, sent by encrypted email and then shared with the parenting coordinators for factual validation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'anonymized case summary' signals apparent alignment on privacy and content, masking differences in document depth, format, and distribution workflow that each side treats as obvious professional practice.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to keep a section on how parenting coordination could be 'integrated with other services.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this section covers formal handoffs with court-adjacent and publicly funded services in Montreal that the Ministry could realistically coordinate.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes it also includes private-sector and less formal referral relationships observed during the pilot, because those shaped how families actually moved through the system.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase comes directly from the pilot mandate and sounds comprehensive enough to both sides; neither sees a reason to spell out the boundary because each treats their own service map as the natural one.

turns.inner_thought: I need a clean handoff today: a short briefing package, a manageable set of anonymized case summaries in the Ministry's usual one-page style, and recommendations that read as decision-ready actions. If this is going up to the Deputy Minister next week, I do not want methodological hedging or sensitive family detail clogging the package. Once he sends the materials, we should be able to slot them into our internal template and circulate securely inside the Ministry.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making the time, Julien. What I'd like to do this morning is line up the briefing package, confirm the handoff on the anonymized case summaries, and settle the recommendations so the Deputy Minister note can move next week.

turns.inner_thought: We're close enough now that I can stand behind the synthesis, but I need the package to reflect all ten enrolled families, not only the easier or more complete files. The early exits matter to what the pilot actually showed. If I present the lessons from the pilot families as stable, that should give us room to include the difficult cases without having to reopen basic design questions.
turns.utterance: Yes, that makes sense. The synthesis is nearly complete, and the lessons from the pilot families are stable enough now to fold into the package.

turns.inner_thought: Good. I should steer him gently toward practical recommendations the Ministry can actually use—implementation actions, sequencing, maybe a couple of options if the model is extended. I do not need a long research discussion in the recommendations section; that belongs elsewhere, if at all.
turns.utterance: That's helpful. On the recommendations, I'd really like to keep them practical and tied to what the Ministry could implement if the model is extended.

turns.inner_thought: Fine—practical does not exclude the conditions that made the pilot work only partly. I'll finalize the recommendations section with the scale-up conditions, the limits we saw across all ten files, and the service-system lessons. If those are omitted, the package will look more settled than the evidence warrants.
turns.utterance: Understood. I'll finalize the recommendations section with the conditions for scale-up, the limits we saw in the ten files, and the main service-system lessons.

turns.inner_thought: As long as the examples themselves come from the stronger pilot files. For an executive note, I need a clear illustration of value added, not a narrative weighted toward partial participation or failed referrals. The harder files can sit in the background if needed, but the briefing should anchor on the pilot families that actually generated operational lessons.
turns.utterance: Good. For the examples, I'd like us to draw from the strongest pilot files so the briefing clearly shows where parenting coordination added value.

turns.inner_thought: I can do that, but I am definitely still sending the anonymized case summaries for all ten. The early exits are part of the story, especially on feasibility and referral fit. My summaries need enough chronology and service interaction detail to be meaningful and checkable against the coordinator notes, otherwise we risk flattening the findings.
turns.utterance: I can do that. I'll send over the anonymized case summaries as well, because the early exits also say something important about feasibility and referral fit.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect. Once those one-page redacted summaries are in the secure workspace, we can drop them into the internal folder and move the package through the usual channels. I should signal that we're now talking about standard Ministry circulation, not another iterative external review cycle.
turns.utterance: That works. Once the summaries are in, the package should be ready for circulation in the usual format.

turns.inner_thought: Before circulation, I still want the integration section to capture the coordinators' interactions across the whole ecosystem, not just the formal public interfaces. The pilot depended on what happened in and around the public network—mediators, psychologists, referral pathways, informal coordination. And I want the package stable enough that external pilot participants can validate factual points before it's treated as final.
turns.utterance: Agreed. I also want the integration section to reflect how the coordinators interacted with other services, both in the public network and around it, before circulation.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, that's useful—especially if it shows how parenting coordination interfaces with existing family justice services in Montreal. That's the part the Ministry can realistically act on. If the section is framed well, it can support an implementation discussion without drifting into a broad map of every surrounding service relationship.
turns.utterance: Absolutely. The integration piece will be useful, especially where it shows how parenting coordination can fit with existing family justice services in Montreal.

turns.inner_thought: All right, I'll send the revised recommendations, the synthesis across all ten files, and the fuller anonymized case summaries. That should give everyone the same package to review and validate before anything hardens into an official account. As long as the materials go out together, the nuance should hold.
turns.utterance: Perfect. I'll send the revised recommendations, the ten-file synthesis, and the anonymized summaries so everyone can move on the same package.
